headline: IN EVERYDAY CONSUMER GOODS, NINE OF EVERY TEN YOUTUBE VIDEOS AN AI ENGINE PUTS IN FRONT OF A SHOPPER CAME FROM AN INDEPENDENT CREATOR RATHER THAN A BRAND, AND A VIDEO'S VIEW COUNT PREDICTS GETTING PICKED AT ALMOST EXACTLY ZERO

tldr: In everyday consumer goods, nine of every ten YouTube videos an AI model surfaces come from independent creators rather than brands, long-form takes 94 percent of YouTube citations against 5.7 for Shorts, and a video's view count predicts being cited at -0.03 while description length predicts it at 0.31.  Rewrite the descriptions on your ten most useful videos this week as a real account of their contents with chapter timestamps, and brief your next creator video as a long-form comparison that names competing products at eight minutes or more.

Since 24 August a YouTube view has meant the first frame played, including an autoplay on a homepage hover, and across more than 75,000 videos the public number sits 1.67 times above the old engaged-views number — rising to plus 85 percent on channels under 50,000 subscribers, with feed autoplay alone accounting for 77 percent of the gap.  Write engaged views into your next creator contract as the reported metric, ask for the Analytics screenshot at delivery, and draw a line across your own branded-video benchmarks at 24 August.

DoubleVerify's 22,000-consumer survey reports social purchasing down to 25 percent from 30 and influencer influence down to 48 from 54, while the same pair of surveys has YouTube usage jumping from 72 percent to 95 and three other platforms moving twenty-odd points each, which no real-world change produces.  Ask for the 2025 question wording before letting the decline near a budget, and use the within-wave figures instead — short-form prompts action for 49 percent in Latin America and 47 in Asia Pacific against 27 in North America.

Google Ads now lets you cap a channel's spend as a percentage of daily budget, but only on a best-effort basis, and Demand Gen — the product that buys YouTube and Shorts — gets the priority switch with no percentage ceiling at all.  Set a defensible percentage ceiling on your Performance Max campaigns this week after writing down today's figures, and diarise January 2027 to set display to low priority at 50 percent on every Search campaign that uses it before Google migrates them in February.

On YouTube's television screens, advertising on the smallest fifth of channels by session size held eyes 48 percent of the time against 41 percent on the largest fifth, and co-viewing ran the other way at 53 against 71 — the people, not the content, are the variable.  Put a real slice of your next television-screen YouTube buy on specialist channels with small average audiences, judge the halves separately on eyes-on-screen, and ask every attention vendor who owns them now.

Aion 2's launch drew 262,150 peak viewers and 16.99 million hours on Twitch off 4,025 simultaneous channels, second only to Fortnite all time, with exactly one named streamer clearing 30,000 — breadth, not stars.  Ask for peak concurrents, average concurrents, airtime and the channel count including co-streams on every live proposal, and get the per-language and per-platform split for the League of Legends World Championship now, in its first week, while inventory is unsold.

TikTok's microseries push produced a first series with more than 580 million views and a follow-up running 68 episodes to roughly one hour with poppi and Sol de Janeiro written into the plot, because a 90-second episode has no break to put an advertisement in.  Script a brand story as 20 vertical episodes of about 50 seconds, each ending mid-decision with the product doing something in the plot, and judge it on how many viewers reach the final episode.
